the large wafer within high applied pressure would exhibit the high stresses possible to cause delamination/failure, and reducing the Cu thickness can diminish the delamination/failures.

the low-k material can be protected by reducing the applying pressure and copper thickness, and the slurry would be a minor effect to delaminate or not the low-k material.
the delamination/failures are mainly caused by the high stresses at the interface, and the warpage induced from the thin-film process is the main reason for the high stress at the interface.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the warpage induced stresses and the applied pressure during the CMP process are the two main causes of the delamination failure.
the warpage induced from the thin-film deposition and the mechanical polishing process would cause high stresses to the wafer, which can lead to delamination of the interface.
the delamination/failures of the low-k materials could be prevented by the reduction in the warpage, applying pressure, and the increase in the copper thickness.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the warpage of the blanket wafer and copper thickness are the key factors for the delamination of the low-k materials during the CMP process.
the delamination of the interface between the copper and low-k material is highly dependent on the warpage of the wafer and the applied pressure of the CMP process.
the delamination of the interface can be prevented by the appropriate selection of the fabrication process conditions.
